description: Full pipeline: video → reversed frames → BunnyCDN upload → sliding window scroll animation

tasks.title: Verify FFmpeg is installed
tasks.notes: Requires ffmpeg >= 4.0. Install via: brew install ffmpeg (mac) or apt install ffmpeg (linux)

tasks.title: Analyze source video
tasks.notes: Confirm duration, fps, resolution, codec. Expected: ~12s, 60fps

tasks.title: Read BunnyCDN credentials
tasks.notes: Storage zone ID should be 1342426 as stated

tasks.title: Create local output folder for frames
tasks.notes: This is where the reversed 24fps WebP frames will be saved locally before upload

tasks.title: Reverse the video and extract frames at 24fps as WebP
notes: reverse: reverses the entire video in memory before processing — requires enough RAM for full video
fps=24: outputs exactly 24 frames per second (~288 frames for a 12s video)
quality 75: targets ~20-40KB per frame. Adjust up/down if frames are over 40KB
If video is long and reverse causes memory issues, use step 2.1b instead

tasks.title: [ALTERNATIVE] Reverse via pts trick if memory is an issue
tasks.notes: Use this only if step 2.1 crashes due to memory. Less reliable but avoids loading full video into RAM

tasks.title: Verify frame count and average file size
tasks.command: ls /home/jaime/Downloads/trophyframes/output_webp/ | wc -l && du -sh /home/jaime/Downloads/trophyframes/output_webp/ && find /home/jaime/Downloads/trophyframes/output_webp/ -name '*.webp' -exec du -k {} + | sort -n | tail -5
tasks.notes: Expected: ~288 frames. Check largest frames. If any exceed 40KB, reduce quality in step 2.1

tasks.title: [CONDITIONAL] Re-encode frames that exceed 40KB
tasks.command: for f in /home/jaime/Downloads/trophyframes/output_webp/*.webp; do size=$(du -k "$f" | cut -f1); if [ $size -gt 40 ]; then ffmpeg -i "$f" -quality 65 "${f%.webp}_compressed.webp" && mv "${f%.webp}_compressed.webp" "$f"; fi; done
tasks.notes: Only run if step 2.2 shows frames over 40KB. Drops quality to 65 for those specific frames only

tasks.title: Final size audit
tasks.notes: Target: under 10MB total. Under 5MB is ideal for mobile cold load

tasks.title: List current files in BunnyCDN folder to confirm path
tasks.notes: Replace YOUR_STORAGE_API_KEY and YOUR_STORAGE_ZONE_NAME from BUNNYCDN_STORAGE.md. Confirm the path exists before deleting

tasks.title: Delete all files in grcup/frames/trophy_frames_webp/
notes: BunnyCDN supports folder deletion by appending trailing slash
This is irreversible — confirm step 3.1 list looks correct before running

tasks.title: Confirm folder is empty
tasks.notes: Should return empty array [] or 404. If files remain, repeat 3.2

tasks.title: Upload all WebP frames to BunnyCDN
tasks.command: for f in /home/jaime/Downloads/trophyframes/output_webp/*.webp; do filename=$(basename $f); curl -s -X PUT -H 'AccessKey: YOUR_STORAGE_API_KEY' -H 'Content-Type: image/webp' --data-binary @"$f" "https://storage.bunnycdn.com/YOUR_STORAGE_ZONE_NAME/grcup/frames/trophy_frames_webp/$filename"; echo "Uploaded: $filename"; done
notes: Uploads sequentially. For faster upload use xargs -P 8 to parallelize 8 at a time
BunnyCDN Storage API rate limit: generous, parallelism is fine

tasks.title: [FASTER ALTERNATIVE] Parallel upload with xargs
tasks.command: ls /home/jaime/Downloads/trophyframes/output_webp/*.webp | xargs -P 8 -I {} sh -c 'filename=$(basename {}); curl -s -X PUT -H "AccessKey: YOUR_STORAGE_API_KEY" -H "Content-Type: image/webp" --data-binary @{} "https://storage.bunnycdn.com/YOUR_STORAGE_ZONE_NAME/grcup/frames/trophy_frames_webp/$filename" && echo "Done: $filename"'
tasks.notes: 8 parallel uploads. Reduce -P value if you hit rate limits

tasks.title: Verify upload count matches local frame count
tasks.command: curl -s -H 'AccessKey: YOUR_STORAGE_API_KEY' 'https://storage.bunnycdn.com/YOUR_STORAGE_ZONE_NAME/grcup/frames/trophy_frames_webp/' | python3 -c "import sys,json; data=json.load(sys.stdin); print(f'Files on CDN: {len(data)}')"
tasks.notes: Count should match local frame count from step 2.2

tasks.title: Purge BunnyCDN pull zone cache
tasks.notes: Uses Account API Key (different from Storage API Key). Pull zone ID found in BunnyCDN dashboard. Ensures CDN edge nodes serve new frames immediately

tasks.title: Implement frame URL helper
tasks.notes: Adjust padding and naming to match what FFmpeg generated in step 2.1

tasks.title: Implement sliding window cache with eviction
Implement initial preload gate
tasks.notes: Block scroll interaction until first 60 frames are ready. Show a progress indicator or freeze on frame 0.

tasks.title: Add preload link in HTML head for first frame
tasks.notes: Tells browser to fetch frame 0 at highest priority before JS even runs

tasks.title: Test on desktop Chrome — check RAM in DevTools
tasks.notes: Open DevTools > Memory tab. Heap should stay under 600MB during scroll. Watch for leaks on repeated scroll up/down

tasks.title: Test on Safari iOS (real device, not simulator)
tasks.notes: Simulator does not enforce real memory limits. Must test on physical iPhone. Enable Safari Web Inspector via Settings > Safari > Advanced

tasks.title: Test cold load in incognito / private tab
tasks.notes: Verify loading overlay shows correctly, first 60 frames load before scroll is enabled, no blank canvas flashes

tasks.title: Test fast scroll (fling) behavior
tasks.notes: Animation should catch up smoothly due to MAX_FRAME_JUMP clamp. Should not crash, freeze, or show blank frames

tasks.title: Verify frame count and ordering (reversed correctly)
tasks.notes: Frame 0001 should be the last frame of the original video. Frame 0288 should be the first frame of the original video
